intent.summary: P9B-4 emergency batch (8 commits, 3a929b6..cbc701b): add a project-level access guard (UserProject grant) to ~20 logistics endpoints/paths in pcs-backend (streams read/write, state points, the 6 state-transition endpoints, stream batch submit, lineage), plus the new guarded endpoint GET /streams/{id}/review-log (TODO-112), plus the prerequisites that make the guard usable (POST /projects auto-grants the creator; scripts/seed_user_project_access.py) and a strict_client pytest fixture that does not mock the guard (the legacy client fixture mocks it to always-True, so guard defects were invisible to it). Guard semantics: no grant => a 404 byte-identical to 'does not exist' (never 403, so UUIDs cannot be enumerated); the guard must run before any business gate. No alembic/versions changes; the bare OpenAPI payload count must not rise above 71.

requirements: T0: project creators are auto-granted access on POST /projects; a seed script grants existing users (mock login creates no users row).
T1: a strict_client test fixture that exercises the real project guard (legacy client mocks it to always-True).
T2: project guards on the logistics read/write endpoints (10 endpoints).
T3: project guards on the 6 state-transition endpoints; the guard runs before the composition gate.
T4: project guard on the batch endpoint; cross-project items are reported as 'does not exist'.
T5: lineage guard extended from a PipingResult-only special case to a record-type registry (streams included).
T6: new guarded endpoint GET /streams/{id}/review-log (TODO-112); read-only, backend-side filtering, named schema ReviewLogItem.
T7: contract roll-forward (openapi baseline), PCS-UI-SPEC 7.7.2 revision (V2.11), TODOS.md, .wolf buglog + cerebrum.
Global constraints: no worktree, no detached HEAD, no alembic/versions changes, bare payload count <= 71, no passwords on the command line, one commit per task, T6 must be independently revertible.

settled_decisions: 404 (not 403) for unauthorized, byte-identical to 'does not exist' so UUIDs cannot be enumerated.
The guard must be the outermost check on write endpoints (a 422 business detail would leak cross-project data).
Same-shape 404 for lineage is 'no lineage for record' - the repo's existing check_record_access_or_404 ('Project not found') was rejected because its envelope differs.
review-log filtering is backend-only (one source of truth); the frontend's own filtering was deleted.
No new index for the review-log query (the existing GIN jsonb_path_ops index cannot serve the ->> predicate); TODO-104 records this.
The legacy 'client' fixture keeps mocking the guard; migrating the whole suite to strict_client is TODO-128.
Pre-existing ruff debt in user_project_service.py is deliberately untouched (TODO-130) per the 'do not fix unrelated code' rule.

Targeted verification actually executed by the dispatch context: `pytest tests/api/v1/test_stream_review_log.py tests/api/v1/test_lineage_guard.py` = 12 passed (the batch's own suite is green, which is itself the evidence that it does not cover the two P1s); frontend `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` clean; `check_openapi_payload_coverage.py` RC 0 with 「当前: 71 个裸 object/array」 (baseline <= 71 holds). The full backend suite was started but hit the 1800 s timeout before it finished, so no independent full-suite number is claimed here; the batch's own recorded figure is 5528 passed / 0 failed.

Important caveat about the batch's own QA evidence: the browser regression in .gstack/qa-reports/qa-report-pcs-frontend-2026-11-09-stream-guard.md exercised the frontend dev server with MSW mocks, so the 200 for GET /api/v1/streams/s-101/review-log and the two rendered rows came from the mock, not from the real backend. That mock data does not match what the real backend produces (see the review-log action-filter finding).

Dispatch-context empirical reproduction (not a persona finding): a standalone probe (dispatch-context-probe-reviewlog.txt, run outside the repo tree, nothing in the project mutated) inserted audit rows using the REAL action values from state_machine.TRANSITION_AUDIT_ACTION and the REAL detail shape from state_machine._write_audit, then called app.services.stream_review_log_service.list_review_log. Result: the four rows written were RECORD_TRANSITION/SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK, APPROVAL_STEP_PASSED/PASS_CHECK, APPROVAL_STEP_REJECTED/REJECT_CHECK and RECORD_TRANSITION/MARK_STALE; the service returned 1 item (SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK) and dropped PASS_CHECK and REJECT_CHECK. VERDICT: BUG REPRODUCED.

Dispatch-context empirical reproduction #2 (not a persona finding): a second standalone probe (dispatch-context-probe-lineage.txt) called the lineage endpoints as a user holding a grant only for project A. Result: for a stream that exists in project B, /upstream, /graph and /downstream all answered 404 {'code':'HTTP_404','message':'no lineage for record'}; for a UUID that does not exist at all, /upstream answered 200 [] while /graph and /downstream answered the same 404. The 404-vs-200 divergence on /upstream is an existence oracle.
